items.q: There are 3 bundles of ten sticks and 4 single sticks. How many sticks are there altogether?
items.hint: Count the bundles in tens (10, 20, 30), then count on the singles.

slips.say: 7 is 3 + 4. A bundle is worth ten, not one. Count the bundles in tens first.
43 is 4 tens and 3 ones. You have 3 bundles and 4 singles, so the 3 goes first.

tpl.q: There are {t} bundles of ten sticks and {o} single sticks. How many sticks are there altogether?
tpl.hint: Count the bundles in tens, then count on the {o} singles.

items.q: How many full bundles of ten can you make from 47 sticks?
items.hint: 47 is made of tens and ones. The left digit counts the tens.
steps: Each ten is one full bundle.
So you can make 4 full bundles.

slips.say: 7 is the number of singles left over. The question asks for the full bundles of ten.
47 is all the sticks. How many tens are in 47?

tpl.q: How many full bundles of ten can you make from {n} sticks?
tpl.hint: The left digit of {n} counts the tens.
steps: {n} is made of tens and ones.
The left digit counts the full bundles.
So you can make {ans} full bundles.

items.q: You tie 47 sticks into bundles of ten. How many single sticks are left over?
items.hint: The right digit counts the ones, the sticks that are not in a bundle.
steps: The 7 ones are left over as singles.

slips.say: 4 is the number of bundles. The question asks for the singles left over.

tpl.q: You tie {n} sticks into bundles of ten. How many single sticks are left over?
tpl.hint: The right digit of {n} counts the ones.
steps: {n} is made of tens and ones.
The tens are tied in bundles.

items.q: Write the number: 9 ones and 2 tens.
items.hint: The tens digit goes on the left, even though the question says the ones first.

slips.say: 92 is 9 tens and 2 ones. The question says 9 ones and 2 tens, so the 2 goes on the left.

tpl.q: Write the number: {o} ones and {t} tens.
tpl.hint: The tens digit goes on the left, even though the question says the ones first.

items.q: Write the number: 7 tens and 0 ones.
items.hint: No ones means the ones digit is 0. The 0 keeps the 7 in the tens place.
steps: There are no ones to add.

slips.say: 7 would be 7 ones. 7 tens needs a 0 in the ones place.
Check the tens: how many bundles of ten is that? Then think about the ones.

tpl.q: Write the number: {t} tens and 0 ones.
tpl.hint: No ones means the ones digit is 0.
steps: There are no ones to add.

items.q: Which number is 4 tens and 6 ones?
items.hint: The tens digit goes on the left and the ones digit on the right.
steps: The left digit 4 counts the tens, the right digit 6 counts the ones.

slips.say: 64 is 6 tens and 4 ones. We need 4 tens first.

items.q: Mei has 5 bundles of ten and 14 loose sticks. How many sticks does she have?
items.hint: Tie 10 of the loose sticks into another bundle. How many bundles and singles now?
steps: 14 loose sticks make 1 more bundle and 4 singles.
Now Mei has 5 + 1 = 6 bundles and 4 singles.

slips.say: 19 is 5 + 14. Bundles are worth ten each, so think of 5 tens first.
Do not join the numbers side by side. 5 bundles is 50, then add the 14.

tpl.q: Mei has {t} bundles of ten and {o} loose sticks. How many sticks does she have?
tpl.hint: Tie 10 of the loose sticks into another bundle.
steps: {o} loose sticks make 1 more bundle and {r} singles.
Now Mei has {u} bundles and {r} singles.

items.q: 41 = 4 tens and 1 one. 41 = 3 tens and how many ones?
items.hint: Opening a bundle gives you 10 more singles. You still have the 1 you started with.
steps: Open one bundle: 3 bundles are left.
The opened bundle gives 10 singles, plus the 1 single you had.
10 + 1 = 11 ones, so 41 is 3 tens and 11 ones.

slips.say: 10 is the opened bundle. Do not forget the 1 single you already had.
1 is the single you started with. The opened bundle gives 10 more.

tpl.q: {n} = {t} tens and {o} ones. {n} = {u} tens and how many ones?
tpl.hint: Opening a bundle gives you 10 more singles. You still have the {o} you started with.
steps: Open one bundle: {u} bundles are left.
The opened bundle gives 10 singles, plus the {o} you had.

items.q: My tens digit is more than 3. My ones digit is 6. I am between 30 and 50. What number am I?
items.hint: List the numbers between 30 and 50 that end in 6. Then check the tens digit of each.
steps: Between 30 and 50 and ending in 6: 36 and 46.
36 has 3 tens, which is not more than 3. 46 has 4 tens, which is more than 3.

slips.say: 36 has 3 tens, and 3 is not more than 3. Check clue 3.

items.q: Mei has 7 tens and 2 ones. Ali has 6 tens and 12 ones. Who has more?
items.hint: Tie 10 of Ali's 12 ones into a bundle. What does Ali have now?
steps: Ali's 12 ones make 1 bundle and 2 ones.
So Ali has 7 tens and 2 ones.
That is the same as Mei: 72.

slips.say: 12 is a big number of ones, but ten of them make a bundle. Tie them up and compare again.

items.q: Ben has 6 bundles of ten and 14 loose sticks. Siti has 85 loose sticks. How many more sticks does Siti have than Ben?
items.hint: Find Ben's number first. Then compare tens and ones.
steps: Ben: 6 tens and 14 ones is 7 tens and 4 ones, which is 74.
85 is 1 ten and 1 one more than 74, so Siti has 11 more.

slips.say: 14 is Ben's loose sticks. Find Ben's whole number (74) first.
25 is 85 - 60. Ben also has 14 loose sticks.

tpl.q: Ben has {t} bundles of ten and {o} loose sticks. Siti has {s} loose sticks. How many more sticks does Siti have than Ben?
tpl.hint: Find Ben's whole number first, then compare it with {s}.
steps: Ben has {t} tens and {o} ones. Tie up ten of the ones to find his number.

items.q: A shop sells pencils in boxes of ten. Mei needs 60 pencils. She has 4 full boxes and 18 loose pencils. How many more pencils does she need?
items.hint: Find how many pencils she has now. Then see how far it is from 60.

slips.say: 18 is the loose pencils she already has. Add the 4 boxes first (40).
42 is 60 - 18. She also has 4 full boxes.

tpl.q: A shop sells pencils in boxes of ten. Mei needs {N} pencils. She has {b} full boxes and {l} loose pencils. How many more pencils does she need?
tpl.hint: Find how many pencils she has now, then see how far that is from {N}.

items.q: How many different ways are there to write 30 as tens and ones? You may open every bundle. (3 tens and 0 ones is one way.)
items.hint: Start with 3 tens and open one bundle at a time.
steps: Open one bundle: 2 tens and 10 ones. Open another: 1 ten and 20 ones. Open the last: 0 tens and 30 ones.

slips.say: There are more ways between 3 tens and 0 tens. Open the bundles one at a time.
Count 0 tens and 30 ones too.

tpl.q: How many different ways can you show {n} with bundles of ten and loose sticks, if you may open bundles?
tpl.hint: Start with all the tens. Open one bundle at a time until there are none left.
steps: Start with the full tens of {n}.
Open one bundle at a time until there are no bundles left.

items.q: Make your own mystery number puzzle with 3 clues: between which two numbers, the ones digit, and a clue about the tens digit, like more than 6. Check that only 1 number fits.
items.hint: Pick a secret number first. Then write clues that are true for it.
steps: Check your secret number fits every clue.
List the numbers that fit the first two clues. Cross out any that break clue 3.
Only one number should be left. For example: between 60 and 80, ones digit 3, tens digit more than 6. That leaves 63 and 73. Only 73 has more than 6 tens, so 73 fits.
